subject: Retention TTL for live sessions vs persisted outputs — clarification
messages:
From: Thomas Nguyen <thomas.nguyen@brightbank.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: BrightBank Security <security@brightbank.com>
Date: 2028-10-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Clarifying default retention for interactive sessions and persisted artifacts

Karthik —

Thanks for taking this. We're updating BrightBank's vendor assessment and have a couple of specific questions about Redwood's default retention behavior. A short list below; we can jump on a call if needed.

1) By default, how long are raw requests (customer prompts) and model responses retained in hosted accounts? Are streamed token fragments treated differently (e.g., fragments buffered for the session only)?
2) How does Redwood distinguish "prompts" (customer inputs) vs "outputs" (model answers) for retention purposes? Any examples would help.
3) Are derived artifacts (embeddings, transcripts, searchable indexes) retained on a different TTL than raw requests/responses?
4) For EU customers who set residency to EU, are all artifacts (requests, responses, derivatives, audit logs) kept only in EU regions by default?
5) What is the standard erasure workflow and SLA when a customer requests deletion of an account's data? How do we provide proof of deletion for procurement?

We appreciate concise answers we can paste into our security questionnaire. I attached our questionnaire template to this thread.

Best,
Thomas
Director, Security Engineering — BrightBank
[attachment: brightbank-questionnaire-template.xlsx (XLSX, 54KB)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Thomas Nguyen <thomas.nguyen@brightbank.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-10-18T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarifying default retention for interactive sessions and persisted artifacts

Thomas —

Appreciate the clear questions. Below is a concise, copy-ready summary you can drop into your questionnaire. I included short clarifying notes at the bottom for any follow-ups.

Short answers (defaults for hosted accounts unless customer configures otherwise):

- Raw requests (prompts) and final model responses: default TTL = 30 days. These are retained to support debugging, billing reconciliation, and quality monitoring.
- Streaming token fragments / live session buffers: ephemeral; kept only for the duration of the session plus a small buffer window (default 2 hours) and not written to long-term stores unless the customer explicitly enables session transcription or logging.
- KV cache and runtime-only artifacts: ephemeral; TTL = 1 hour by default and purged automatically by the runtime.
- Derived artifacts (embeddings, transcripts, indexes): default TTL = 365 days; these are treated as persisted assets and can be configured per-account.
- Audit logs and deletion evidence: audit records of erasure actions and the deletion job run logs are retained for 365 days by default (separate from request/response TTLs) to provide proof-of-deletion.
- Residency: when an account is configured with EU residency, primary storage for requests, responses, and persisted derivatives is constrained to EU regions by default. Replication to non-EU regions does not occur unless the customer explicitly enables cross-region backups.
- Erasure workflow & SLA: customer can initiate deletion via Console or API. Hosted accounts: deletion jobs are queued and generally complete within 72 hours; confirmation and an audit artifact (signed deletion token + job id) are available via the Console and Delivery API. Dedicated/Private: deletion requires coordination with Customer Success and support; SLA negotiated per contract.

Notes / Examples:
- Example: If a customer uses real-time chat but doesn't enable transcript persistence, the streamed tokens are dropped after the 2-hour buffer and do not become part of the 30-day request/response store.
- Example: If you enable index creation over conversations, the embeddings created for that index will live per the 365-day TTL unless you set a custom retention or delete the index.

Attachments: I attached a short one-page summary (PDF) and a completed version of your questionnaire (see attached).

Open to a quick call if you'd like to walk this through with compliance.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference

Thanks — that helps a lot. A couple quick follow-ups:

- For the 30-day request/response TTL, is the deletion a logical delete (soft-delete) followed by physical purge? What's the timeline for full physical removal?
- For proof-of-deletion, can you provide an example of the audit artifact format? Our procurement requires an attestation with a job id and timestamp.
- Does Redwood treat model outputs that include user PII (if present in the response) any differently in retention or handling?

If it's easier, Monica or Kimberly can add any compliance-level specifics.

Thanks — Thomas

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Thomas Nguyen <thomas.nguyen@brightbank.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-10-20T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarifying default retention for interactive sessions and persisted artifacts

Thomas — quick add from Security & Ops: 

- Deletion semantics: hosted accounts perform a two-step deletion for requests/responses: 1) logical delete (immediate marking) and removal from active queryable stores; 2) background physical purge job which completes within 7 days for the vast majority of records (and up to 30 days in edge cases where archived backups are involved). We provide the deletion job id and a signed audit token after the job completes.
- Proof artifact: we deliver a JSON-structured deletion receipt (example attached in Drive link) that includes account id, deletion job id, start/end timestamps (ISO8601), checksum of purged blobs, and the operator/service that executed the run. The delivery is accessible via the Console and can be included in an automated webhook.
- PII in outputs: we do not apply different retention TTLs automatically based on content sensitivity — retention is policy-driven (account-level setting). That said, customers in regulated industries frequently configure shorter TTLs or enable automatic redaction transforms prior to persistence. We can also offer an add-on erasure verification report for regulated customers.

Action items: 
- Karthik: I'll drop the deletion receipt example into the Drive link and attach a one-page attestation template.
- Monica/Kimberly: We'll prepare a short note for procurement describing the hosted deletion SLA and the artifact format.

Thanks — happy to run a live demo of the deletion request flow if you want.

—Monica Patel
Director, Security & Trust — Redwood Inference
